summary: Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and Oxford, completing her doctorate under Jonathan A. Silk (2010–2015). She held posts as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden (2015–2016) and research fellow at Heidelberg University.

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott and Albrecht Weber. He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg (1867) and served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz, Wilhelm Grube, and August Conrady, graduating from Leipzig. He held posts at Columbia University (~1905–1907) and the Field Museum (~1908–1934).

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Salzburg and with Lakshman Joo. She held directorships at the Alice Boner Institute and Abhinavagupta Research Library, and was a professor at Vienna (~1997).

Bettine Birge is a Sinologist and historian. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University (~1982–1989) under Robert P. Hymes and William Theodore de Bary, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Bonn, Kiel, and Halle-Wittenberg. She held academic posts at the University of Kiel (~1923–1931), Halle-Wittenberg (~1931–1933), SOAS University of London (~1934–1945), and the University of Hamburg.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.
Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a linguist and Indologist. He served as a professor at Osmania University (~1962–1986) and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Study (~1999–2000).

Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his M.A. from the University of Calcutta (~1887). He served as Honorary Secretary of the Board of Trustees and Managing Committee at Central Hindu College (~1899–1914).

Bhajagovinda Ghosh works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Assistant Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and as an editorial board member of the Bulletin of Tibetology in 1994.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Agra University. He has held positions at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied under Bhikkhu Bodhi, at the University of Ceylon, and Marburg. He held posts at Marburg, Hamburg, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, and Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy.

Bhikkhu Bodhi works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Brooklyn College, Claremont Graduate University, and under Balangoda Ananda Maitreya and Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984) and held a post at Chuang Yen Monastery (~2006).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After studying at Magadh University (~1968–1974), he held posts at the University of Kassel, the University of Bergen, and served as professor at the University of Marburg (~1995–2004).
Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā is a Buddhist studies scholar. She held posts at Dharma Drum Buddhist College as an assistant researcher (~2012–2014) and at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (~2014).
Bhuvan Chandel is an Indologist and philosopher. She served as a professor at Panjab University (~1968–2002) and as Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (~2000–2003).

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, W. V. O. Quine, and Dagfinn Føllesdal. He held posts at Calcutta, Toronto, and as a professor at Oxford (1976).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of London. He was professor and department head at Patna University (~1953–1979) and honorary joint director at Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (~1968–1977).
Bing Chen works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held appointments as a professor at Sichuan University (~1987) and at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences.
Bintao Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at Peking University and a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (~2010–2015).
